documents.title: Institutional AI Policy
documents.stance_why: The policy is a framework: it "embraces the transformative potential" of AI and sets principles, but says "Operational requirements, permitted uses, prohibited uses ... are set forth in the AI Acceptable Use Policy" and points to the faculty and student guidance, so it sets no stance on student AI use itself and delegates.
documents.summary: UNE's overarching AI policy sets definitions, nine guiding principles (do no harm, integrity, transparency and so on) and a governance committee. It states no rule for coursework itself and sends operational rules to the AI Acceptable Use Policy and the faculty and student guidance.

units.why: The introduction states the institution's purpose for the whole policy: "foster the appropriate, responsible, and ethical use of AI tools", which is an institution-level framework, so P56, general, informs.
units.anchor: UNE seeks to foster the appropriate, responsible, and ethical use of AI tools

units.why: "remains fundamentally human-centered" states a guiding principle of the whole framework, so P56 general informs. P87 does not fit because no benefit is named here.
units.anchor: educational environment remains fundamentally human-centered

units.why: "provides the overarching framework" with detail left to other documents sets the scope and layering of the policy set, so P56.
units.anchor: This Institutional AI Policy provides the overarching framework for AI use at UNE.

units.why: The sentence names AI as "Any machine-based system that autonomously performs tasks commonly associated with human intelligence": a definition setting policy scope, so P61.
units.anchor: Any machine-based system that autonomously performs tasks commonly associated with human intelligence
units.frag_end: based on a set of objectives
units.policy: Artificial intelligence (AI) means any machine-based system that autonomously performs tasks commonly associated with human intelligence or generates outputs such as predictions, recommendations, or decisions based on a set of objectives.

units.why: Defines agentic AI as "Autonomous systems designed to pursue complex goals with minimal human intervention", a definition that sets what the policy covers (P61).
units.anchor: Autonomous systems designed to pursue complex goals with minimal human intervention.
units.policy: Agentic AI means autonomous systems designed to pursue complex goals with minimal human intervention.

units.why: Defines generative AI and says it "includes both standalone offerings and offerings that are embedded in other software", which sets scope (P61). P07 is not chosen because it gives no rule about editors or agents.
units.anchor: Generative AI includes both standalone offerings and offerings that are embedded in other software.
units.fit_note: Also brings AI embedded in other software within scope, which touches P07, but states no rule about it.

units.why: Defines "Enterprise private AI tools" as "licensed, contractually protected, and approved by the University", a term that sets the line between sanctioned and public tools (P61).
units.anchor: AI tools that are licensed, contractually protected, and approved by the University
units.frag_start: Enterprise private AI tools: AI tools that
units.frag_end: no model training on University data
units.policy: Enterprise private AI tools are AI tools that are licensed, contractually protected, and approved by the University, with guarantees of data isolation, no external access, and no model training on University data.

units.why: Defines "High-risk data" as data requiring "the highest level of protection" including FERPA records, which fixes the scope of the privacy rules (P61).
units.anchor: Data that requires the highest level of protection, including Protected Health Information (PHI)
units.policy: High-risk data is data that requires the highest level of protection, including PHI, FERPA student education records, PCI and financial data, PII, or confidential organizational information.

units.why: Defines "Publicly available AI tools" as tools used "without UNE vetting, procurement, or approval", the scope term for unvetted tools (P61).
units.anchor: AI tools that are accessible to the general public via the internet
units.frag_start: Publicly available AI tools: AI tools
units.policy: Publicly available AI tools are AI tools accessible to the general public via the internet, without UNE vetting, procurement, or approval.

units.why: Principle 1 says AI "must be used in ways that protect privacy, security, and equity for all UNE community members", an ethical-use principle (P53), not a rule on coursework.
units.anchor: must be used in ways that protect privacy, security, and equity for all UNE community
units.policy: must be used in ways that protect privacy, security, and equity for all UNE community members
units.fit_note: Also covers privacy and equity, not only harms.

units.why: Under Do No Harm, members are asked to be "cautious about what information is entered into AI systems" and to choose tools that protect data, which is P50.
units.anchor: choosing tools that protect personal and institutional data, being cautious about what information is entered
units.policy: choosing tools that protect personal and institutional data, being cautious about what information is entered into AI systems

units.why: The same principle requires "promptly reporting any concerns about misuse, safety, or potential harm", a reporting duty matching P71.
units.anchor: promptly reporting any concerns about misuse, safety, or potential harm

units.why: Principle 2 says "Users are responsible for ethical AI use and for the actions and outcomes", i.e. ownership of results (P29).
units.anchor: Users are responsible for ethical AI use and for the actions and outcomes that result
units.policy: Users are responsible for ethical AI use and for the actions and outcomes that result from using AI tools.

units.why: "being honest about when and how AI has been used" is a disclosure duty for all members, so P24.
units.anchor: being honest about when and how AI has been used
units.fit_note: Framed as honesty in general, with no specific statement or citation form.

units.why: "correcting errors introduced by AI" tells users to fix AI mistakes before relying on them, P31 (verify output).
units.anchor: correcting errors introduced by AI

units.why: "seeking guidance when unsure about appropriate use" tells members to ask when unsure, P10.
units.anchor: seeking guidance when unsure about appropriate use

units.why: Principle 3 expects members to be "open about when and why AI tools are used" and to avoid "secret or hidden use of AI where it affects others", a transparency duty (P24).
units.anchor: avoiding secret or hidden use of AI where it affects others
units.fit_note: A general transparency duty to all community members, not tied to a submission.

units.why: Principle 4 "encouraged to share effective practices, lessons learned, and concerns about AI use across departments" is internal peer exchange, nearest P88; the type is about outside partners so this fits only partly.
units.anchor: encouraged to share effective practices, lessons learned, and concerns about AI use across departments and
units.policy: encouraged to share effective practices, lessons learned, and concerns about AI use across departments and roles
units.fit_note: Internal sharing across departments, not coalitions with outside bodies.

units.why: Principle 5 asks for "meaningful options to participate or opt out" of AI, a choice-and-autonomy rule that matches no listed type well.
units.anchor: offering, where feasible, meaningful options to participate or opt out
units.uncovered_note: Respect for autonomy: people should be offered options to participate in or opt out of AI use affecting them and have their preferences honored.

units.why: Principle 5 also says members "should provide and seek clear information about when AI is being used", a right-to-know rule matching P103.
units.anchor: provide and seek clear information about when AI is being used and what choices are
units.policy: provide and seek clear information about when AI is being used and what choices are available

units.why: Principle 6 says "using approved tools for sensitive data", directing users to vetted tools for protected data (P50).
units.anchor: using approved tools for sensitive data, limiting the sharing of identifiable or confidential information

units.why: Principle 6 requires "reporting any suspected privacy or security issues promptly", an incident-reporting duty (P71).
units.anchor: reporting any suspected privacy or security issues promptly

units.why: Principle 6 requires following "institutional policies and legal requirements" for data, which is P77.
units.anchor: following institutional policies and legal requirements

units.why: Principle 7 asks members to "consider the potential impacts of AI tools before and while using them", including "assessing when human review is necessary", a risk-weighing duty that fits no listed type.
units.anchor: consider the potential impacts of AI tools before and while using them
units.uncovered_note: Members must weigh benefits and risks of an AI use before and during use, decide when human review is needed, and stop uses with unacceptable risk.

units.why: Principle 8 says members are "encouraged to engage in training", pointing to AI training for the whole community (P70).
units.anchor: All community members are encouraged to engage in training, reflect on their experiences
units.frag_end: improve policies, tools, and practices over time

units.why: Principle 8 says UNE "commits to ongoing learning, reflection, and refinement of AI practices", so the policy will change (P54).
units.anchor: UNE commits to ongoing learning, reflection, and refinement of AI practices

units.why: Principle 9 tells members to "avoid using AI in ways that deceive, manipulate, harass, or harm others", a conduct ban matching P74.
units.anchor: avoid using AI in ways that deceive, manipulate, harass, or harm others

units.why: Principle 9 asks members to decline AI uses that "bypass meaningful learning and professional responsibilities", a rule that people keep doing the learning themselves; nearest P32 (stay the primary problem-solver).
units.anchor: bypass meaningful learning and professional responsibilities
units.fit_note: Also covers declining uses that reinforce bias, erode trust or obscure accountability.

units.why: "embraces the transformative potential of artificial intelligence" states an institution-level welcoming stance on AI in education, research and administration, so P02 (permit or encourage by default).
units.anchor: embraces the transformative potential of artificial intelligence
units.fit_note: Institutional embrace of AI; it does not set a default for any specific coursework.

units.why: The statement lists "opportunities to improve learning, increase efficiency, support innovation, and expand access", naming benefits without making a rule (P87).
units.anchor: AI technologies offer significant opportunities to improve learning, increase efficiency, support innovation

units.why: "Faculty, professional staff, and students are expected to follow these standards, ensuring both legal compliance" binds everyone to the standards and to law (P77).
units.anchor: Faculty, professional staff, and students are expected to follow these standards

units.why: "UNE’s AI Governance Committee ... provides institutional oversight" names who oversees standards and tool approvals, P80.
units.anchor: UNE’s AI Governance Committee, in collaboration with academic and administrative leaders, provides institutional oversight

units.why: The committee also handles "enterprise AI tool approvals", i.e. review and approval of tools before deployment, P65.
units.anchor: oversight for AI-related governance, standards, and enterprise AI tool approvals

units.why: "regularly reviewing and updating its policies" states the policy will be revisited as technology changes, P54.
units.anchor: regularly reviewing and updating its policies to reflect technological advances, regulatory changes

units.why: The section sends the detailed rules to another document: "Operational requirements, permitted uses, prohibited uses ... are set forth in the AI Acceptable Use Policy", an institution-wide scope statement (P56).
units.anchor: Operational requirements, permitted uses, prohibited uses, data protection requirements, and compliance expectations are set forth
units.policy: Operational requirements, permitted uses, prohibited uses, data protection requirements, and compliance expectations are set forth in the AI Acceptable Use Policy.

units.why: "will be reviewed at least annually" fixes a review cycle, P54.
units.anchor: This policy will be reviewed at least annually and updated as needed

documents.title: AI Policy Guidance for Faculty
documents.stance_why: It says "a single uniform approach to AI use is not practical" and that "faculty have flexibility", requires each syllabus to state a policy, and offers three templates ("AI Use Restricted", "AI-Integrated with Some Restrictions", "Open Use of AI Permitted") that are "a recommended starting point rather than required language", so the stance is delegates with tiers.
documents.summary: Guidance telling UNE faculty to put an AI policy in every syllabus, explain it to students, and disclose their own AI use. It offers three optional syllabus templates (restricted, integrated with restrictions, open) with shared wording on disclosure, accuracy, privacy and misuse, and advises against relying on AI detectors.

documents.title: AI Policy Guidance for Students
documents.stance_why: It says "Your instructor determines how AI may be used" and lists three course approaches ("Restrict AI use", "Integrate AI with some restrictions", "Permit open use of AI"), with the default "assume that its use is not permitted" only when an assignment is silent, so the document delegates to instructors and lists tiers.
documents.summary: Guidance for UNE students explaining that each course sets its own AI rules but four expectations hold everywhere: disclose and cite, own the work, protect privacy and IP, and expect discipline for misuse. It also covers approved versus public tools, research use, detectors, accommodations and where to ask for help.

notes: Coder A. Coded three university-layer documents. The AI Acceptable Use Policy and Research Guidance were not collected, so rules they hold are not coded here. Template wording shared across the three faculty templates was coded once (shared core) and tier-specific wording separately. Several units carry fit_notes where the type fits only partly; UNCOVERED units: opt-out autonomy, weigh risks before use, instructors not letting personal opinions override, meeting students at their AI skill level, template-design rationale.
